title: PSN02 customer due diligence
rule_text: Covered DPT providers need customer and beneficial owner identification controls. Periodic account review is also described by MAS.
applicability_notes: Covered digital payment token service providers under MAS PSN02; confirm licence and activity scope.
example_query: Are customer and beneficial owner checks sufficient for this Singapore DPT customer?

title: PSN02 suspicious activity monitoring
section: Notice overview: monitoring and suspicious transaction reporting
rule_text: MAS describes monitoring and suspicious transaction reporting among DPT provider controls. Investigate unusual activity rather than treating amount or wallet type alone as proof of suspicion.
applicability_notes: Covered digital payment token service providers under MAS PSN02; confirm licence and activity scope.
example_query: A Singapore DPT transfer is unusual for this customer. What monitoring obligations should be reviewed?

title: PSN02 record keeping
rule_text: Record keeping forms part of PSN02 AML/CFT requirements. Determine the required records and retention rules from the current notice; this overview does not establish a retention period.
applicability_notes: Covered digital payment token service providers under MAS PSN02; confirm licence and activity scope.
example_query: Which records should a Singapore DPT provider retain for this case?

title: PSN02 risk assessment and mitigation
section: Notice overview: risk assessment and risk mitigation
rule_text: PSN02 includes risk assessment and mitigation, plus internal compliance policies, audit and training. Review whether the provider's controls address the identified money laundering and terrorist financing risks.
applicability_notes: Covered digital payment token service providers under MAS PSN02; confirm licence and activity scope.
example_query: Which Singapore AML/CFT controls need review for a high-risk DPT relationship?

title: Virtual currency transfer information
rule_text: Covered financial entities, MSBs and foreign MSBs include originator and beneficiary name, address and account or reference information where applicable with outgoing VC transfers. Incoming transfers requiring a VC record need reasonable measures to obtain the information.
applicability_notes: Covered Canadian reporting entities; check entity type, direction, record trigger and exceptions in the cited guidance.
example_query: Which originator and beneficiary information is needed for a Canadian VC transfer?

title: Missing transfer information
rule_text: When required transfer information is absent, take reasonable measures to obtain it. Document risk-based policies for allowing, suspending or rejecting the transfer if information remains unavailable; missing data does not by itself establish a universal rejection requirement.
applicability_notes: Covered Canadian reporting entities; check entity type, direction, record trigger and exceptions in the cited guidance.
example_query: A received Canadian VC transfer lacks beneficiary data. Must it always be rejected?

title: Large virtual currency receipts
rule_text: Reporting entities assess receipts equivalent to CAD 10,000 or more for LVCTR reporting, including relevant exceptions. The guidance also applies a consecutive 24-hour aggregation rule. A receipt threshold is not a blanket outgoing-transfer prohibition.
applicability_notes: Covered Canadian reporting entities; check entity type, direction, record trigger and exceptions in the cited guidance.
example_query: Does a CAD 12,000 virtual currency receipt require an LVCTR assessment?

title: Consecutive 24-hour aggregation
rule_text: Related VC receipts may meet the CAD 10,000 reporting threshold in a consecutive 24-hour window. Check the specified person, entity, third-party or beneficiary linkage and exceptions using the full guidance before grouping transactions.
applicability_notes: Covered Canadian reporting entities; check entity type, direction, record trigger and exceptions in the cited guidance.
example_query: Several related Canadian VC receipts total CAD 11,000 within 24 hours. Which reporting rules apply?

title: Virtual currency sanctions scope
rule_text: OFAC sanctions also cover virtual currency where U.S. jurisdiction applies. Review the applicable sanctions program and authorizations before determining whether dealings are prohibited.
applicability_notes: Persons and transactions within applicable OFAC jurisdiction; assess program, ownership and authorization.
example_query: Does OFAC sanctions compliance apply to a US-linked virtual currency transfer?

title: Risk-based sanctions screening
section: Sanctions compliance best practices: sanctions screening
rule_text: OFAC recommends risk-based screening controls using available customer and transaction information. Investigate potential matches and relevant restrictions; a similarity score alone is not a confirmed sanctions designation.
applicability_notes: Persons and transactions within applicable OFAC jurisdiction; assess program, ownership and authorization.
example_query: A US-linked wallet has a potential sanctions screening match. What needs investigation?

title: Blocked entity ownership
rule_text: Entities owned 50 percent or more in aggregate, directly or indirectly, by blocked persons can themselves be blocked even without a separate list entry. Ownership analysis is necessary; screening only listed names can miss exposure.
applicability_notes: Persons and transactions within applicable OFAC jurisdiction; assess program, ownership and authorization.
example_query: An unlisted counterparty is partly owned by blocked persons. Which ownership controls apply?

title: Convertible virtual currency business classification
section: Administrators and Exchangers of Virtual Currency
rule_text: Administrators or exchangers accepting and transmitting or buying and selling convertible virtual currency may be money transmitters, subject to limitations or exemptions. A user purchasing goods or services with their own CVC is distinguished from such business activity.
applicability_notes: Business-model classification under FinCEN guidance; assess exemptions and current requirements.
example_query: Does a US convertible virtual currency exchange business fall under money transmitter rules?
